packet.background: The exact September Employment Situation summary, released 2 October, is retained. Payroll employment is the establishment survey; unemployment and participation are household-survey measures. Store the prior payroll and revision observations separately from the future October print.
comparison_plan: At T0 retain current October, prior September as first observed, and any newly revised prior values in separate columns.
Do not mix payroll job changes with household employment changes or unemployment-rate percentage-point movements.
Verify exact table units and seasonal-adjustment labels before admitting a numeric chart; no missing cells are imputed.

Newly captured A-1/B-1 raw tables confirm the prior headline direction and survey separation; retain preliminary flags and March 2025 benchmark note. Do not turn a raw B-1 cell into jobs without admitted unit metadata.
missing_inputs: Actual October release and revision vintage at T0

prior_fact_spans.exact_source_span:
Both nonfarm payroll employment (+29,000) and the unemployment rate (4.2 percent) changed little in 
September, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Employment in all major industries 
changed little over the month.
prior_fact_spans.metric: September payroll change and unemployment; reported units jobs and percent

prior_fact_spans.exact_source_span:
This news release presents statistics from two monthly surveys. The household survey measures labor 
force status, including unemployment, by demographic characteristics. The establishment survey 
measures nonfarm employment, hours, and earnings by industry. For more information about the 
concepts and statistical methodology used in these two surveys, see the Technical Note.

The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for July was revised down by 31,000, from +21,000 to 
-10,000, and the change for August was revised down by 29,000, from +162,000 to +133,000. With 
these revisions, employment in July and August combined is 60,000 lower than previously reported. 
(Monthly revisions result from additional reports received from businesses and government agencies 
since the last published estimates and from the recalculation of seasonal factors.)

packet.release_clock_basis: Retained release-specific official schedule plus newly retained BLS annual calendar statement that all calendar times are Eastern; 08:30 EST is 13:30 UTC and 20:30 GMT+7 on these November dates. Scheduled time is not actual publication or known-at.

Admit only the bounded new facts; native Light preparation then same MAX writing/final rendered review and sole coordinator. This packet allocates no operation, fetch budget or publication.

packet.title: Employment Situation for October2026, 6 November
update_frames: Report the actual October headline and revision totals separately; state whether revisions reinforce or weaken the apparent direction only after comparison.
If payroll and household measures diverge, explain distinct survey populations and uncertainty; do not reconcile by inventing a cause.
Use a wage/hours or industry frame only if actual components materially change the reader conclusion.
watchpoints: October payroll change separately from September/August revisions; preserve originally reported and revised values with their vintages.
Household unemployment, participation and employment-population ratio separately from establishment payroll jobs.
Hours, earnings and industry breadth; source adjustment labels and uncertainty before a chart or claims of trend.
No market-surprise or policy-path conclusion from a print alone; expectations and price reaction are separate evidence.
